blocks.text: I can say what someone else and I want to do on a summer trip to Lanzarote using ‘querer’.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A verb meaning to want, wanting.
I want. Part of the verb querer.
You want. Part of the verb querer.
She, he, it wants. Part of the verb querer.

blocks.text: Lucas and Sam read a book of trabalenguas (tongue twisters). Reciting tongue twisters is a good way of practising sound-spelling correspondences and pronunciation.

items: Tres tristes tigres tragan trigo en un trigal. = Three sad tigers swallow wheat in a wheat field.
Cómo poco coco como, poco coco compro. = As I eat little coconut, I buy little coconut.
Pablito clavó un clavito. = Pablito nailed a tiny nail.
¿Qué clavito clavó Pablito? = What tiny nail did Pablito nail?
El clavo quedó clavado. = The nail stayed nailed.
¡Claro! Lo clavó Pablito. = Of course! Pablito nailed the tiny nail.

blocks.text: In Spanish, the ‘v’ is a ‘b’ sound. Say [que] as in ‘queso’ and [v] as in ‘ver’.
Start slowly and get faster and faster!

blocks.q: Match each line of the tongue twister to its English.

pairs.b: What tiny nail did Pablito nail?
Of course! Pablito nailed the tiny nail.

blocks.text: Revisiting vocabulary helps develop confidence and communication. Match the Spanish and English.
Sofía says what she wants to do. Look where the describing word (adjective) goes.

items: Quiero ir a un jardín {bonito}. = I want to go to a beautiful garden.

blocks.label: What do you notice?
blocks.text: In English the adjective comes before the noun: a **beautiful** garden. In Spanish, many adjectives come **after** the noun: un jardín **bonito**.
Adjectives also agree with the gender and number of the noun they describe.

items: Quiero comer la comida rápida. = I want to eat fast food.
Quiero visitar los puertos viejos. = I want to visit the old ports.

blocks.text: When we describe more than one person or animal, we add **-s** after -o, -a and -e.

blocks.q: Choose the adjective that agrees with the noun.
Which noun would each adjective describe: a masculine one (un/el) or a feminine one (una/la)?

blocks.text: The verb querer means to want, wanting. It does not follow the general rules: ‘quer-’ changes to ‘quier-’.
Querer is followed by the **infinitive**. Example: Quiere visitar el teatro grande. = She wants to visit the big theatre.
Let’s translate: ‘I want to visit a quiet village.’

items: Step 4: the adjective goes after the noun: **tranquilo**.

items.q: I want to see the famous volcano.
You want to try a big paella.
I want to eat fast food.

blocks.text: In Lanzarote there is a national park with a volcano: el parque Timanfaya. The Jameos del Agua are famous caves. The typical food is papas arrugadas, which you can try with the sauce ‘mojo picón’.

blocks.q: What is the national park with the volcano in Lanzarote called?
blocks.why: En el parque Timanfaya hay un volcán. The Jameos del Agua are famous caves, and papas arrugadas is typical food.

items: Reciting tongue twisters is a good way of practising sound-spelling correspondences and pronunciation.
Revisiting vocabulary helps develop confidence and communication.
Many adjectives follow the noun and agree in gender and number with the noun they describe.
Querer means to want, wanting: **quiero** (I want), **quieres** (you want), **quiere** (she, he, it wants), followed by an **infinitive**.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Lanzarote in summer: translate sentences with ‘querer’ from memory
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a short answer. Write the Spanish words in lower case. Remember: many adjectives come after the noun.

questions.prompt: Write in English: ‘Pablito clavó un clavito’.
questions.explanation: This is the first line of the Pablito tongue twister.

questions.prompt: Write in English: ‘El clavo quedó clavado’.
questions.explanation: This is the third line of the Pablito tongue twister.

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: ‘I want to visit an important theatre’.
accepted: yo quiero visitar un teatro importante
questions.explanation: Quiero + the infinitive visitar, then the noun un teatro, then the adjective after it.

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: ‘You want to try a big paella’.
questions.explanation: Quieres means ‘you want’. The adjective grande goes after the noun paella.

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: ‘You want to go to quiet cities’.
questions.explanation: Cities is plural, so the adjective adds -s: tranquilas. It goes after the noun.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct adjective ending: ‘los puertos viej___’. Write the whole adjective.
questions.explanation: Puertos is masculine and more than one, so viejo becomes viejos.

questions.prompt: Do most adjectives come before or after the noun in Spanish? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: Many adjectives follow the noun: un jardín bonito.

questions.prompt: Write in Spanish: ‘I want to visit a quiet village’.
accepted: yo quiero visitar un pueblo tranquilo
questions.explanation: Quiero + the infinitive visitar, then un pueblo, then the adjective tranquilo after the noun.

questions.prompt: Which national park in Lanzarote has a volcano? Answer with one word.
questions.explanation: En el parque Timanfaya hay un volcán.
